verdict.line: You lose this by trading autos into his Infected Cleaver range all lane; you win it by collapsing with Shadow Dash the moment he overextends, since Shen holds the measured solo-kill edge.

brief.thesis: Dr. Mundo's Q (Infected Cleaver, 975 range, 4s cooldown, damage scaled off your max health) outranges Shen's entire kit, including Vorpal Blade's 475 range, which is why this sits at only 42.5% across 193 games even though OP.GG calls the lane shape even. Shen's real edge isn't the poke war, it's the skirmish: Shadow Dash's taunt punishes any step Mundo takes into its 575-range path, and the data backs Shen for solo kills. The lane is won by refusing the ranged chip trade and waiting for the one window Mundo gives up himself.

theirWindow.what: Don't stand at your own Q's max range to answer his — his Infected Cleaver hits from nearly double that distance on a 4s cooldown. Shove the wave with minions as cover and let Second Wind heal the chip instead of trading auto for auto.

yourWindow.when: He pushes up without minion cover
yourWindow.what: Dash in with E (Shadow Dash) to taunt him on the way through, then stack Q (Vorpal Blade) and autos — Shen carries the measured solo-kill advantage in this matchup, so this is the fight to take, not the poke war.

start.why: 66.4% pick rate at 43.7% win rate — the flat damage block and regen directly answer a laner whose only early tool is a repeated max-health-scaling poke.

boots.why: Measured at 52% win rate over 98 games versus Plated Steelcaps' 39.8% — Mundo has no hard disable to dodge, so the raw stat return and tenacity against ignite/CC from the rest of the enemy team wins out.

core.why: First item on the strongest measured path (57.1% win rate over 14 games), and the max-health scaling keeps your trades relevant against his own health-scaling Cleaver.
Second item on that same path — keeps the build on the highest-sampled winning sequence.
Completes the top-winrate path and directly answers OP.GG's own tip: Mundo's Adrenaline Rush and Sadism regen collapse against grievous wounds.

situational.when: he's rushing you down early and you need the grievous wounds component before Thornmail finishes
their comp has heavy magic damage stacked behind Mundo
the game goes long and you need more raw health to keep tanking objectives
your team wants a zone-control teamfight item over a second anti-heal piece

runes.keystoneWhy: The highest-sampled page (37.3% pick, 50% win rate) — Grasp's max-health scaling and sustain are built for exactly this kind of long poke lane against a health-stacking Cleaver.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is the dominant pick (66% pick rate, 45.7% win rate) and it's the right tool here specifically: Ignite's burn cuts straight through Adrenaline Rush's passive regen during the skirmish windows where Shen already holds the solo-kill edge.

playing.title: Respect Cleaver's range
playing.detail: Infected Cleaver hits from 975 range on a 4s cooldown while Vorpal Blade only reaches 475 — don't walk up to answer his poke with your own, you'll just eat two of his for every one of yours.

playing.title: Punish overextensions with E
playing.detail: Shadow Dash taunts any champion it passes through on its way to the target point. The moment Mundo pushes past minion cover, dash through him to lock the taunt before he can turn and burn you down with Q.

playing.title: Track his Sadism timer
playing.detail: Sadism is a 75s cooldown panic button that trades his own health for speed and heavy regen. All-in right after he's used it, not while it's up and ready to bail him out.

playing.title: Rush grievous wounds by item three
playing.detail: Thornmail on the top-winrate build path exists specifically to shut down Adrenaline Rush and Sadism — don't delay it chasing damage items once he starts outscaling your poke trades.

playing.title: Life-tap and disengage
playing.detail: Vorpal Blade heals you on the trade, but its cooldown (6s down to 4s at rank 5) is slower than his Cleaver's flat 4s — land your Q and back off, don't stand and auto through his next one.

playing.title: Save W for a stacked Cleaver
playing.detail: Feint's shield is your answer to a big max-health Q hit — time it to absorb the cleaver itself, not the auto attack that follows.

playing.title: Use R to leave a stale lane
playing.detail: Stand United's long cooldown (200s down to 160s) teleport lets you abandon a losing poke war and swing a fight elsewhere instead of forcing trades you're statistically behind in.

brief.patchCaveat: All win rates, pick rates, item paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are this brief's own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of being punished by Dr. Mundo’s cleavers (Q). Purchase items that reduce healing to greatly decrease Dr. Mundo’s laning abilities. Use [E] to engage whenever Dr. Mundo steps in range.
